note.text: In negative sentences, all partitives become de. Ex: Je ne mange pas de pommes.

info_boxes.label: Subject + Verb + Object + Adverbial
info_boxes.fr: Je parle français tous les jours.

question_words.note: Use Que at the start of a sentence. Use Quoi after a preposition or at the end.

question_structures.label: Yes/No Question
question_structures.en: Place at the start to form a question.
question_structures.example: Est-ce que tu aimes le café ?

info_boxes.label: Affirmative
info_boxes.example: Il y a un chat. / Il y a des chats.

info_boxes.label: Negative
info_boxes.example: Il n'y a pas de chat.

info_boxes.label: Must / Must Not (Infinitive)
info_boxes.fr: Il faut / Il ne faut pas
info_boxes.example: Il faut étudier. (One must study.)

info_boxes.label: Should (Advice - Conjugated)
info_boxes.example: Tu devrais manger. (You should eat.)

info_boxes.label: Direct Object (COD) — replaces a noun directly
info_boxes.fr: me, te, le/la, nous, vous, les
info_boxes.example: Je le vois. (I see him/it.)

info_boxes.label: Indirect Object (COI) — replaces à + noun
info_boxes.fr: me, te, lui, nous, vous, leur
info_boxes.example: Je lui parle. (I speak to him/her.)

note.text: Placement: Object pronoun goes BEFORE the conjugated verb. In negation: Je ne le vois pas.

info_boxes.label: y
info_boxes.body: Replaces à + place or location. Use to avoid repeating a place.
info_boxes.example: J'y vais. (I am going there.)

info_boxes.label: en
info_boxes.body: Replaces de + noun, quantities, or partitive phrases.
info_boxes.example: J'en veux. (I want some.)

info_boxes.label: Quantity with en
info_boxes.body: When you keep a quantity, en comes before the verb.
info_boxes.example: J'en ai trois. (I have three of them.)

note.text: In negation, y and en stay before the verb: Je n'y vais pas. Je n'en veux pas.

info_boxes.label: Comparative of superiority
info_boxes.body: Use plus ... que to compare two things.
info_boxes.example: Elle est plus grande que moi.

info_boxes.label: Comparative of inferiority
info_boxes.body: Use moins ... que.
info_boxes.example: Il est moins rapide que toi.

info_boxes.label: Comparative of equality
info_boxes.body: Use aussi ... que to show equality.
info_boxes.example: Il est aussi intelligent que son frère.

info_boxes.label: Superlative
info_boxes.body: Use le/la/les plus or moins to show the extreme degree.
info_boxes.example: C'est la plus belle maison.

info_boxes.label: Qui
info_boxes.body: Used for the subject of the relative clause.
info_boxes.example: La fille qui parle est française.

info_boxes.label: Que
info_boxes.body: Used for the object of the relative clause.
info_boxes.example: Le livre que je lis est bon.

info_boxes.label: Dont
info_boxes.body: Replaces de + noun in the relative clause.
info_boxes.example: Le garçon dont je parle est ici.

info_boxes.label: Où
info_boxes.body: Used for place or time.
info_boxes.example: La ville où j'habite est belle.

info_boxes.label: Note
info_boxes.body: Relative pronouns connect two clauses and provide extra information about a noun.
info_boxes.example: C'est le film que j'ai vu hier.

info_boxes.label: Form
info_boxes.body: The past participle agrees with the subject in gender and number.
info_boxes.example: Le livre est lu par Marie.

info_boxes.label: Usage
info_boxes.body: Use for emphasis on the action or the receiver of the action.
info_boxes.example: La lettre est écrite par Paul.

info_boxes.label: Ne ... jamais / plus / rien
info_boxes.body: These add nuance: never, no longer, nothing.
info_boxes.example: Je ne mange jamais de viande. Je n'en mange plus. Je ne vois rien.

info_boxes.label: Ne ... personne / aucun
info_boxes.body: Used with people or none/any.
info_boxes.example: Je ne vois personne. Je n'ai aucun problème.

info_boxes.label: Structure
info_boxes.body: Most advanced negations still use ne + verb + second negative element.
info_boxes.example: Il n'a invité personne. (He invited no one.)

info_boxes.label: Auxiliary: AVOIR
info_boxes.body: Used for 95% of verbs (the "default").

info_boxes.label: Auxiliary: ÊTRE
info_boxes.body: Used for Movement and Pronominal verbs.

children.title: 14 Verbs of Movement (Être) ✈️
children.note: *Note: These verbs require gender/number agreement (e.g., allé vs. allée).

children.title: 14 Essential Pronominal Verbs 🧘
children.note: Reflexive actions always use être in Passé Composé.

info_boxes.label: Use for...
info_boxes.body: Habitual/repeated past actions, background descriptions, ongoing states in the past, and interrupted actions.

info_boxes.label: Endings (same for ALL verbs)
info_boxes.body: -ais, -ais, -ait, -ions, -iez, -aient

note.text: Passé Composé vs Imparfait: Use PC for completed single events. Use Imparfait for ongoing background states. Example: Il pleuvait (Imp.) quand je suis sorti (PC).
Key Irregular Stems: être→ser-, avoir→aur-, aller→ir-, faire→fer-, pouvoir→pourr-, vouloir→voudr-, venir→viendr-

sections.title: Conditionnel Présent
sections.subtitle: Use to express polite requests, wishes, or hypotheticals.

info_boxes.label: Formation
info_boxes.body: Use the future stem + imparfait endings. This is the polite hypothetical form.
info_boxes.example: Je parlerais si j'avais le temps. (I would speak if I had time.)

info_boxes.label: Usage
info_boxes.body: Use for polite requests, wishes, or actions that depend on a condition.
info_boxes.example: Je voudrais un café. (I would like a coffee.)

note.text: Common structure: si + imparfait, then conditionnel présent. Example: Si j'étais riche, j'achèterais une maison.

sections.title: Conditionnel Passé
sections.subtitle: Used for past hypothetical or regret.

info_boxes.label: Form
info_boxes.body: Use conditional avoir or être + past participle.
info_boxes.example: J'aurais mangé si j'avais eu faim. (I would have eaten if I had been hungry.)

info_boxes.label: Meaning
info_boxes.body: Expresses what would have happened in the past under a different condition.
info_boxes.example: Elle serait venue si elle avait su. (She would have come if she had known.)

note.text: The auxiliary verb is chosen the same way as in passé composé: avoir or être.

sections.title: Subjonctif Présent
sections.subtitle: Used after necessity, emotion, doubt, or will.

info_boxes.label: Trigger expressions
info_boxes.body: After expressions like il faut que, je veux que, je doute que.
info_boxes.example: Il faut que tu viennes. (You must come.)

info_boxes.label: Common verbs
info_boxes.body: Used with vouloir, souhaiter, craindre, regretter, être content que.
info_boxes.example: Je souhaite que tu sois ici. (I wish that you were here.)

note.text: The subjunctive is not a tense of time; it expresses attitude, desire, doubt, or necessity.

sections.title: Subjonctif Passé
sections.subtitle: Used for past actions after subjunctive triggers.

info_boxes.label: Form
info_boxes.body: Use the present subjunctive of avoir or être + past participle.
info_boxes.example: Je suis content que tu aies réussi. (I am happy that you succeeded.)

info_boxes.label: Example
info_boxes.body: Use when the action is completed in a subordinate clause after a subjunctive trigger.
info_boxes.example: Je doute qu'il ait fini. (I doubt that he finished.)

note.text: Remember: the auxiliary is in subjunctive present, not indicative.

info_boxes.label: Tip
info_boxes.body: No subject is used in the imperative. Use tu, nous or vous only to show who is addressed.
info_boxes.example: Va à l'école. (Go to school.)

info_boxes.label: -ER verbs
info_boxes.body: For tu form of -er verbs, drop the final 's' unless it is followed by y or en.
info_boxes.example: Mange ! / Va !

info_boxes.label: Negative form
info_boxes.body: Use ne ... pas around the verb in negative commands.
info_boxes.example: Ne parle pas ! (Don't speak!)

sections.title: Passive Voice
sections.subtitle: Use être + past participle to focus on the receiver of the action.

info_boxes.label: Form
info_boxes.body: Subject + être + past participle + par + agent (optional).
info_boxes.example: Le gâteau est mangé par les enfants. (The cake is eaten by the children.)

info_boxes.label: Agreement
info_boxes.body: The past participle agrees with the subject in gender and number.
info_boxes.example: La lettre est écrite. Les lettres sont écrites.

info_boxes.label: When to use it
info_boxes.body: Use passive voice when the doer is unknown, unimportant, or when the receiver is the main focus.
info_boxes.example: Cette maison a été construite en 1900. (This house was built in 1900.)

note.text: If the agent is not needed, you can leave out 'par ...'.

note_top.text: The Golden Rule: The word must match the gender and number of the noun that follows it.

note_bottom.text: ⚠️ The "Vowel Rule": If a feminine noun starts with a vowel (like amie), you must use the masculine form: Mon amie (not Ma amie).

sections.title: Adjective Placement & Meaning
sections.subtitle: Learn how position changes meaning and when adjectives come before or after the noun.

info_boxes.label: Standard position
info_boxes.body: Most adjectives follow the noun: un livre intéressant, une femme intelligente.
info_boxes.example: Une voiture rouge.

info_boxes.label: Before noun
info_boxes.body: Some adjectives come before the noun and often change meaning: grand homme vs homme grand.
info_boxes.example: Un grand homme (a great man) vs un homme grand (a tall man).

info_boxes.label: Common pre-nominal adjectives
info_boxes.body: Adjectives like beau, nouveau, vieux, bon, mauvais often precede the noun.
info_boxes.example: Un bon repas, une nouvelle idée, un vieux château.

note.text: Adjective position is a high-level skill in French: it affects nuance, register, and meaning.

sections.title: Adverb Formation & Placement
sections.subtitle: Master how French adverbs are built and where they sit in real sentences.

info_boxes.label: From adjectives
info_boxes.body: Most adverbs are formed from adjectives by adding -ment. If the adjective ends in -ant or -ent, use -amment or -emment.
info_boxes.example: rapide → rapidement, patient → patiemment

info_boxes.label: Position
info_boxes.body: Place manner adverbs after the verb or between auxiliary and past participle in compound tenses.
info_boxes.example: Elle parle doucement. Elle a rapidement fini.

info_boxes.label: Nuance
info_boxes.body: Learn the difference between bon (adjective) and bien (adverb), or rapide and rapidement for more natural phrasing.
info_boxes.example: Il est bon. Il travaille bien.

note.text: Advanced speakers use adverbs to refine tone, rhythm, and register in French.
Adverbs of quantity + Noun must use "de / d'". Ex: Beaucoup d'amis

info_box.title: Expressing Pain
info_box.body:
Structure: Avoir + mal + à (au, à la, à l', aux)

Headache: j'ai mal à la tête
Stomach ache: j'ai mal au ventre
Toothache: j'ai mal aux dents
